question.problem: Suppose that $|\,p\,|=3$, $|\,q\,|=6\sqrt{2}$ and that the angle between the vectors is $\theta =\frac{3\pi }{4}.$ Find the vector projection of $q$ onto $p$ in terms of the vector $p.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the scalar projection as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{p}\,q & =|\,q\,|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =6\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{4}) \\  & =6\sqrt{2}\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =-6\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the unit vector that is parallel to $p:$

$$
u=\frac{p}{|\,p\,|}=\frac{p}{3}=\frac{1}{3}p
$$

Finally, we compute the vector projection as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{p}\,q & ={\text{comp}}_{p}\,q\cdot u \\  & =-6\cdot \frac{1}{3}p \\  & =-2p\end{aligned}
$$
